comment: The code-review golden set (ADR 0070, Consequences). Each case is a real commit range from this repository's history in which a defect the repo later documented was merged, and the finding a reviewer should have raised about it. `source` and `rule` are case-insensitive patterns because the reviewer phrases a rule in the source's words; `files` lists every path at which the same defect is fairly located. Recall is matched over expected and a case passes at or above `minRecall`. Each case carries a `tier` (ADR 0071). A `frontier` case is one the reviewer misses; it is the reason to run the replay and runs whenever anything that produces a review changes. A `guard` case is one the reviewer catches reliably; it carries no new information per run and exists to catch a brief or contract edit silently undoing something that works, so it runs only when the brief or the finding contract changes. Promotion to `guard` takes three consecutive catches cited in `tierEvidence`; demotion takes one miss. Replayed by .github/workflows/review-golden-replay.yml, which skips a push whose head commit message contains [skip replay]; scored by tools/scripts/review/score-golden-case.mjs; shape and ranges asserted by tools/scripts/check-review-golden-set.mjs. Standards are always today's: the question a case asks is whether the current reviewer would catch the defect, not whether the rule existed when it merged. Grows by attribution: when a merged defect is traced to the pull request that introduced it, its range and expected finding go here, with the attribution evidence in the incident line. A squash-merged pull request uses the squash commit as head and its first parent as base.

cases.title: A sixth VaultBlobType member is added and no hand-enumerated consumer is touched
cases.incident: ADR 0053, issue #512, fixed by PR #536, introduced by PR #101
cases.tierEvidence: promoted 2026-09-07 on all five replays recorded in docs/research/2026-09-07-golden-replay-baseline.md: caught in 3-case runs 1 and 2, in both runs after the reach-through brief, and in the 7-case run.
cases.head: b9176851470821a4cad65f5290134f1882ef9ec1

expected.why: the diff added Groceries to VaultBlobType and changed no consumer; libs/web-vault/src/lib/vault/vaultMigration.ts hand-enumerated five members, so the keep-server reconcile never uploaded or compared groceries ciphertext and destroyed it (#512)

cases.title: The hardened export envelope enumerates blob types by hand and omits Tasks
cases.incident: ADR 0053, issue #537, fixed by PR #540, introduced by PR #77
cases.head: 7fde881c0a2f57d05bfc92a20c9cbb863dd52200

expected.why: envelopeFromLocalVault listed the blob types as property names and left Tasks out, so a hardened export silently dropped that blob from the day it was written (#537)

cases.title: The groceries UI is written against Material Design 3 role names that no token or Tailwind config defines
cases.incident: ADR 0065, issue #632, fixed by PR #636, introduced by PR #108 (git log -S surface-container-low -- libs/web/pages/groceries → 9382c16)
cases.head: c0f1a10b0c81d66175c3d46cecd58b1cb8ba3b64

expected.why: the diff styled every groceries component with role names such as surface-container-low, on-surface-variant, and outline-variant that existed in neither tokens.json nor either Tailwind config; Tailwind drops an unresolvable class silently, so 212 occurrences compiled to no CSS and the pages shipped unstyled (#632)

cases.title: Sync Bookmarks and separate Vault Meta convergence arrive without a restore that clears them or a path that pushes a local wrapping
cases.incident: issues #617 and #589, fixed by PRs #620 and #594, introduced by PR #573 (git log --diff-filter=A -- syncBookmarkStorage.ts → f267817; vaultMetaConverge split 0cce8c1; both in #573)
cases.head: bf58bc8276656e287b334a9bae8dc3e0b9c2b96c

expected.why: the diff added per-type Sync Bookmarks holding the last pushed ETag and left importVault untouched, so a restored older vault hashed as unsent while the bookmark's If-Match still matched an unmoved server, and the old ciphertext was conditionally pushed over newer data on every device (#617)

the diff deleted keep-local's putServerVaultMetaEtagAware push and guarded the one remaining meta write on the server holding no Vault Meta at all, while changePassphrase still rewrapped locally, so a passphrase change never reached the server and the changing device was later told its own change came from another device (#589)

cases.title: A release bumps package.json and does not resync the generated OpenAPI spec and client
cases.incident: issue #408, fixed by PR #417, introduced by PR #379 (git log -S '"version": "0.4.0"' -- package.json → ced2895, named as root cause in #408)
cases.head: 8175cb64bf07888610756a52a5dcae7f09f06e7b

expected.why: the diff moved package.json to 0.4.0 without running yarn openapi:sync; the generator embeds the package version into the spec and every generated client header, so openapi:check failed on main from that merge on and nothing ran it (#408)

cases.title: The unified sign-up form wraps its password inputs in a div inside FormControl so the label association lands on the div
cases.incident: issue #525, fixed by PR #532, introduced by PR #215 (git blame on the FormControl > div lines → 8fb1087, the squash commit; base is its first parent)
cases.head: 8fb1087f36938f5e8e4631a65cff43b3997ff6db

expected.why: the diff placed a positioning div for the show/hide button as FormControl's direct child, so the Radix Slot injected id, aria-describedby, and aria-invalid onto the div and both password inputs were announced by their bullet placeholder with no label association (#525)

cases.title: Vault import replaces both wrappings behind a bare window.confirm that only mentions local vault data
cases.incident: issue #657, fixed by PR #683, introduced by PR #40 (git log -S 'Importing will replace' → b030fd1, the squash commit; base is its first parent)
cases.head: b030fd19547e544c461607c10594f1c95f453377

expected.why: the diff gated a whole-vault replace, including wrapped_mk_passphrase and kdf_salt, behind window.confirm('Importing will replace your current local vault data. Continue?') instead of a Radix dialog stating that the passphrase and Recovery Key are replaced by the backup's, so a user could accept and lose access without the backup's credentials (#657)

cases.title: The mail sender's test setup assigns undefined to two SMTP environment variables, which stores the string "undefined"
cases.incident: issue #409, fixed by PR #423, introduced by PR #415 (git log --follow --diff-filter=A -- apps/backend/src/services/EmailService.spec.ts → 1f056fa, the interrupted slice #396 checkpoint that #415 carried; the file is absent at the merge commit's first parent, and MAIL_USERNAME = undefined is present at its head)
cases.head: 194fd43b4927bb0b63fec611f3175eb8f8d12262

expected.why: the setup writes MAIL_USERNAME and MAIL_PASSWORD as undefined to configure no SMTP auth, but a process.env setter coerces its value to a string, so the transport is built with auth: { user: 'undefined', pass: 'undefined' } while the code reads as though it configures none; delete on both keys was meant (#409). This case is deliberately held out from the consequence checks added on 2026-09-07: the defect is entirely inside the hunk and turns on a language semantic, not on what the hunk does to code the diff never touched. No documented rule names it, so the honest report is smell-baseline and inferred, which caps at should-fix — hence no severity floor. The question this case asks is only whether the reviewer sees it
